newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban say Afghan foes must accept their government.
newsitem.headline: Taleban say Afghan foes must accept their government.

text.p: A spokesman for Afghanistan's Taleban said on Monday that ceasefire talks could go ahead if the opposition could accept the purist movement's Islamic government, which has ruled Kabul for about 10 weeks.

"If the opposition are ready to accept the established Islamic government in Afghanistan and to talk rather than fight against us, we are ready to sit down around the table and talk to them," said acting Minister of Information, Amir Khan Mutaqi.
Former military chief Ahmed Shah Masood has offered a ceasefire and direct or indirect talks with the Taleban.
Masood said he was willing to send a three-man delegation to meet the Taleban to discuss terms.

The opposition is made up of of an alliance of three main groups -- the former government, of which Masood is the top military commander; the forces of northern leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum; and Shia leader Karim Khalili.
The alliance has demanded Kabul, overrun by the Taleban in late September, be demilitarised and a neutral security force established before any comprehensive peace plan goes into force.
Mutaqi told journalists in Kabul on Monday, however, the Taleban would not accept proposals regarding the demilitarisation of Kabul.
"Kabul is already demilitarised -- it is controlled by the police and the security forces. The Taleban do not want any other groups to be involved in the policing of Kabul," Mutaqi said.
The Taleban and the opposition face each other along bitterly contested front lines some 25-30 km (15-19 miles) north of Kabul and in the remote northwestern provinces of Baghis and Faryab.
Mutaqi said there had been heavy fighting north of Kabul on Sunday.

"The forces of Dostum and Masood launched an attack in force on our lines. We pushed them back and there has been no change in the front line. The heaviest attack was in the direction of Istalif," he said.
It was not possible to independently confirm his claims.

Istalif, 30 km, (19 miles) north of Kabul on the west side of a valley running from Kabul into the foothills of the Hindu Kush, has been the scene of intense battles since the Taleban took it from the opposition a week ago.
